title: TCS NQT Prep Guide: What to Study and In What Order
excerpt: A practical study order for TCS NQT-style screening: quant foundations first, reasoning patterns next, then communication and easy coding.
provenance: BountyCode prep strategy. Exam formats change yearly — treat section splits as pattern guidance, not official TCS communication.

sections.heading: How NQT-style screening is built
sections.body: Service-company screening tests check speed and accuracy on school-level quant, logical patterns, verbal communication, and basic coding. Nobody expects hard DSA here. Your edge is finishing easy questions fast without silly mistakes.

sections.heading: Weeks 1–2: Quant foundations
sections.body: Master percentages, ratios, profit/loss, averages, time & work, and time-speed-distance. These six patterns decide most of your quant score. Open each topic's theory card, memorize the 3–4 formulas, then drill 20 timed questions.

sections.heading: Weeks 3–4: Reasoning patterns
sections.body: Blood relations, syllogisms, coding-decoding, directions, seating, and series. Draw every problem — family trees, Venn overlaps, compass grids. Never solve arrangement puzzles in your head.

sections.heading: Week 5: Communication + easy coding
sections.body: Practice the email format until its structure is automatic: subject, greeting, purpose, all prompt keywords, closing. For coding, arrays, strings, and basic loops are enough — solve easy pattern-sheet problems daily.

sections.heading: Final week: Full mocks
sections.body: Take two full timed mocks in the Mock OA section. After each mock, open your weakness diagnosis, complete the repair set, and retest before the next mock. A mock without repair is just a score.

title: Infosys Prep Guide: Pseudo-Code and Puzzles First
excerpt: Infosys-style screening weights logical reasoning and pseudo-code tracing heavily. Study order for maximum score per hour.
provenance: BountyCode prep strategy. Exam formats change yearly — treat section splits as pattern guidance, not official Infosys communication.

sections.heading: What decides your score
sections.body: Infosys-style papers reward careful reading: puzzles, series, syllogisms, and pseudo-code tracing where one missed line costs the question. Accuracy beats attempts here.

sections.heading: First: pseudo-code tracing
sections.body: Practice predicting program output line by line: loops, nested loops, arrays, conditions, functions. Trace with a variable table on paper exactly like the exam demands.

sections.heading: Second: reasoning puzzles
sections.body: Seating arrangements, series completion, coding-decoding, and syllogisms. Learn the seating-arrangement theory card, then drill the Logical Puzzles category until diagrams feel automatic.

sections.heading: Then: quant + technical MCQs
sections.body: Percentages, ratios, averages, and time-work for quant; OOP basics, DBMS, and C fundamentals for technical MCQs. Keep notes on every formula you look up twice.

title: Wipro Prep Guide: Balanced Speed Across Four Sections
excerpt: Wipro-style screening spreads marks across quant, reasoning, verbal, and coding. A balanced 4-week plan with no section left behind.
provenance: BountyCode prep strategy. Exam formats change yearly — treat section splits as pattern guidance, not official Wipro communication.

sections.heading: The balanced-paper problem
sections.body: When every section carries weight, your weakest section caps your score. Diagnose first: take one timed drill in each category and let the weakness report rank them.

sections.heading: Daily rotation
sections.body: Alternate days: quant + verbal one day, reasoning + easy coding the next. Thirty focused minutes per section beats three hours on your favourite topic.

sections.heading: Verbal is free marks
sections.body: Reading comprehension, para jumbles, and sentence correction follow fixed rules. Read each theory card once, then drill — most students gain 15–20% in a week here.

sections.heading: Coding: basics done well
sections.body: Arrays, strings, loops, and functions. Write clean code that compiles first time — Wipro-style coding rounds reward working solutions over clever ones.

title: Accenture Prep Guide: Verbal and Pseudo-Code Decide It
excerpt: Accenture-style screening leans on cognitive ability, verbal fluency, and technical pseudo-code. Where to put your hours.
provenance: BountyCode prep strategy. Exam formats change yearly — treat section splits as pattern guidance, not official Accenture communication.

sections.heading: Verbal first
sections.body: Reading comprehension, sentence correction, and vocabulary carry unusual weight here. The verbal theory cards plus daily timed drills close this gap fastest.

sections.heading: Pseudo-code like Infosys
sections.body: Trace variables, predict output, nested loops, arrays. The same tracing discipline applies — variable table on paper, no mental execution.

sections.heading: Cognitive speed
sections.body: Abstract reasoning and attention-to-detail questions punish hesitation. Drill short timed sets (10 questions, 10 minutes) until your pace stabilises.

sections.heading: Coding round
sections.body: One or two easy-medium problems. Arrays, strings, hashing basics from the pattern sheets are sufficient — finish one clean solution rather than starting two.

title: Cognizant Prep Guide: Accuracy Under Time Pressure
excerpt: Cognizant-style screening is a speed game on familiar patterns. Build a personal formula sheet and automate the easy marks.
provenance: BountyCode prep strategy. Exam formats change yearly — treat section splits as pattern guidance, not official Cognizant communication.

sections.heading: Automate the easy marks
sections.body: Percentages, averages, ratios, and series questions should take under 60 seconds each. If any take longer, that pattern goes on your repair list the same day.

sections.heading: Reasoning without re-reads
sections.body: Coding-decoding, blood relations, and analogies are won by method: positions table for letters, trees for families. One method per pattern, practised until boring.

sections.heading: Mock with a stopwatch mindset
sections.body: In mocks, skip any question that survives 90 seconds and return later. Unattempted beats wrong when negative marking looms — check the mock's rules first.

title: Capgemini Prep Guide: Games, Logic, and Spoken English
excerpt: Capgemini-style screening mixes game-based aptitude with logic and English. How to prepare for each format.
provenance: BountyCode prep strategy. Exam formats change yearly — treat section splits as pattern guidance, not official Capgemini communication.

sections.heading: Game-based rounds
sections.body: Some Capgemini-style rounds use game-like tasks measuring attention, memory, and reactions. You cannot study the games — but daily timed drills train the same calm-under-clock muscle.

sections.heading: Logic core
sections.body: Puzzles, coding-decoding, critical reasoning. Same pattern discipline as everywhere else: diagrams for arrangements, position tables for codes.

sections.heading: Spoken and written English
sections.body: If your round includes spoken English, narrate your mock solutions aloud while practising. For written rounds, the sentence-correction and email theory cards cover the graded parts.

title: HCL Prep Guide: Technical Depth on a Screening Budget
excerpt: HCL-style screening adds technical MCQs to the standard quant-logical-verbal mix. Split your time with intent.
provenance: BountyCode prep strategy. Exam formats change yearly — treat section splits as pattern guidance, not official HCL communication.

sections.heading: The 60-40 split
sections.body: Spend roughly 60% of prep time on quant, reasoning, and verbal (common to every mass recruiter) and 40% on technical MCQs: C output questions, OOP concepts, DBMS basics, networking fundamentals.

sections.heading: C output questions
sections.body: The highest-yield technical topic. Practice predicting output for loops, pointers basics, arrays, and operator precedence — the same tracing skill as pseudo-code rounds.

sections.heading: CS fundamentals as MCQs
sections.body: OS definitions, DBMS keys and normal forms, CN layers. One-line facts, best learned as daily 10-question drills with the explanations read carefully.
